sources.entry: AutoMute - Automatically mute the sound when headphones disconnect / Mac awake from sleep.

summary.one_liner: AutoMute is a macOS menu bar app that automatically mutes system sound when headphones disconnect, the Mac sleeps, or the screen locks or enters the screen saver.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the macOS menu bar and mutes the sound when headphones (including Bluetooth headphones) are disconnected, when the Mac goes to sleep, or when the Mac gets locked or enters the screen saver. It stays active as long as it is running. The README's stated purpose is to prevent playback from blasting at full volume when you open a laptop in a quiet place, or when Bluetooth headphones move out of range and audio switches to the built-in speakers. The README describes only these behaviors and does not list settings or other options.
use_cases: Mute audio when Bluetooth headphones disconnect
Stop music playing when the Mac sleeps
Silence sound when locking the screen
Prevent speakers blasting after walking away from Bluetooth headset
Avoid unexpected loud playback when opening laptop
how_to_run: Install from the Mac App Store (link in README)
Or open the Xcode workspace file in Xcode
stack: Swift/Objective-C (macOS app; language not named in README)
notable: Lives in the macOS menu bar
Handles both wired and Bluetooth headphone disconnects
Mutes on sleep, screen lock, and screen saver
Available on the Mac App Store
caveats: Building from source requires Xcode; the README says 'everything should work' without further guarantees
README does not describe configuration options or a changelog
